entries.title: Attempt on Fluctuations and large deviations of intermediate level sets of the 2D DGFF (corrected)
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD (SUPERSEDING REVISION 2026-09-07 12:4x after the Codex holder's review), author-checked only. CORRECTION of C0002-A001. With Var h_x = g log N + O(1) and threshold 2 sqrt(g) lambda log N, P(h_x >= threshold) = exp(-2 lambda^2 log N)/(sqrt(2 pi) 2 lambda sqrt(log N)) (1 + o(1)), so the mean size of the intermediate level set is of order N^{2 - 2 lambda^2}/sqrt(log N), not a constant times N^{2(1 - lambda^2)} as A001 wrote; the (log N)^{-1/2} is the leading normalisation, not a correction term. The rest of A001 (variance dominated by mesoscopic pairs, mixing-measure identification open) stands with this normalisation. Key identity: E|level set| = c N^{2-2 lambda^2} (log N)^{-1/2} (1+o(1)) with c = 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi) lambda) times the boundary-correction factor. Standing obstruction: see the earlier attempt; the correction above replaces the flawed step only.

entries.title: Attempt on Explicit density of the position of the DGFF maximum (corrected)
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD (SUPERSEDING REVISION 2026-09-07 12:4x after the Codex holder's review), author-checked only. CORRECTION of C0004-A001. The sentence 'the naive guess rho^D proportional to r_D(x)^2 fails unless Z^D(D) is a.s. constant' is too strong: if Z^D = xi mu with xi a random scalar and mu deterministic, then Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D) = mu(dx)/mu(D) is deterministic and E[Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D)] = E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) although Z^D(D) is random. The correct statement: rho^D differs from the normalised intensity E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) exactly when the total mass Z^D(D) is not independent of the normalised measure Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D); for the DGFF extremal measure this independence fails (the mass and the shape are coupled through the Gibbs-Markov structure), so rho^D is not r_D(x)^2 dx normalised, but the argument in A001 does not prove that and the question stands. Key identity: rho^D = E[Z(dx)/Z(D)] equals E Z(dx)/E Z(D) iff the total mass is independent of the normalised measure (sufficient direction), not iff the mass is constant. Standing obstruction: see the earlier attempt; the correction above replaces the flawed step only.

entries.title: Harmonic-mean product-measure domination for equivariant determinantal processes on a finite group
entries.statement: PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT (revision 2), no independent review. Let Gamma be a finite group and Q a Gamma-equivariant positive contraction on l^2(Gamma) with 0 < Q < I, and P_Q the determinantal measure with kernel Q. Let HM(Q) be the harmonic mean of the eigenvalues of Q. Then P_Q stochastically dominates the product Bernoulli measure of density HM(Q), and P_Q is dominated by the product measure of density 1 - HM(I - Q). Precise chain: the minimal conditional ODDS of presence is s_min = 1/(J^{-1})_ee = HM/(1 - HM) with J = Q(I-Q)^{-1}, and the minimal conditional PROBABILITY is s_min/(1 + s_min) = 1/(Q^{-1})_ee = HM(Q) (revision 2 states the odds and the probability separately, after a reviewer noted the two had been conflated in a side note). This is weaker than Lyons's Conjecture 5.7 (geometric mean / Fuglede-Kadison determinant), which numerical monotone-coupling linear programs on Z/nZ, n <= 6, satisfy exactly, with FK + 0.01 failing on a tested instance; those LP results are floating-point evidence, not certificates.
entries.proof_text: Write J = Q(I - Q)^{-1}, so that P_Q(X = A) = det(I - Q) det(J_A). For a site e and configuration B on Gamma minus e, P_Q(e in X | X minus e = B) = s_B/(1 + s_B) with s_B = det J_{B union e}/det J_B = 1/((J_{B union e})^{-1})_{ee}. For positive definite M and S subset S' containing e, ((M_{S'})^{-1})_{ee} >= ((M_S)^{-1})_{ee}, so s_B is nonincreasing in B and its minimum is s_min = 1/(J^{-1})_{ee} = 1/((Q^{-1})_{ee} - 1). Equivariance makes Q a convolution operator diagonalised by the characters, so (Q^{-1})_{ee} = (1/|Gamma|) trace(Q^{-1}) = 1/HM(Q); hence s_min = HM/(1 - HM) and the minimal conditional probability is s_min/(1 + s_min) = HM(Q). Holley's inequality with a product measure as the smaller measure reduces to this one-site condition, so P_Q dominates Bernoulli(HM(Q))^Gamma; the complement process has kernel I - Q, giving the upper domination.
assumptions: Finite group Gamma
Q Gamma-equivariant with 0 < Q < I
Holley's inequality in its product-measure form

entries.title: Lyons's union-marginal coupling question: transportation polytope feasible in every tested instance (floating-point evidence), naive conditional splitting fails
entries.statement: PRIVATE NUMERICAL EVIDENCE (revision 2), not a proof and not an exact certificate. Lyons (ICM 2014, Question 2.8) asks whether for H = H_1 (+) H_2 orthogonal in l^2(E) there is a coupling of P_{H_1} and P_{H_2} whose union has law P_H; the union must be disjoint by cardinality, so the question is the nonemptiness of a transportation polytope with three marginals. A floating-point LP (HiGHS, minimum total violation) reported violation 0.0 on 1360 random instances with |E| in {3,...,6}, on |E| = 7 and 8 generic instances, on Fourier-mode subspaces of cycles and on star-space splits of the K_4 edge space. Revision 2 records the reviewer's point that double-precision feasibility is evidence only; an exact rational LP on rational-kernel instances is the next step. The naive conditional splitting fails to reproduce the P_{H_2} marginal (direct computation on |E| = 4). Open: a general construction.
assumptions: Finite E, orthogonal subspaces
Floating-point evidence only

entries.title: A stationary determinantal process whose symbol is a function of k theta is an interleaving of independent copies on the k residue classes
entries.statement: PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT (revision 2), no independent review. Let f(theta) = g(k theta) for an integer k >= 2 and a symbol g into [0,1]; then the restrictions of the stationary determinantal process P_f to the residue classes kZ + j are independent and each is P_g after reindexing. Consequence for Lyons's Question 5.4: if P_g is an (m/k + 1)-block factor of an i.i.d. process then P_f is an (m + 1)-block factor. Revision 2 corrects the scope: this settles the question only when the reduced symbol g is a proved case, i.e. degree 1 (so f(theta) = a + b cos(m theta) for any m), and NOT all even degrees; for f of degree 4 the reduction produces degree 2, itself open.
entries.proof_text: The Fourier coefficients of g(k theta) vanish off multiples of k, so K(x,y) = f-hat(x - y) = 0 unless x = y mod k; a determinantal measure with block-diagonal kernel is the product of the block measures (all minors factorise and correlation functions determine the law); within a class the kernel is g-hat(x - y). The block-factor consequence: interleave k independent block-factor constructions with independent i.i.d. sequences on the classes; the value at x depends on the window {x, ..., x + m}.
assumptions: f = g(k .) with g a symbol into [0,1]
Block-diagonal kernels give product measures
Settled cases: reduced degree 1 only
